rules.semantic_direction_not_state_change: Louder/quieter ask whether a relative loudness request is expressed. An absolute target without comparative direction does not express either relative request: false under complete review, even though actual physical change is unknown. If the wording itself is ambiguous about relative direction, mark unavailable.
rules.adjustment: Setting/changing output loudness or an explicit mute/unmute control is audio_level_adjust. Requests to speak louder/softer also adjust output loudness. Merely forbidding speech or pausing playback does not explicitly change a loudness control.
rules.silence: audio_silence covers explicitly suppressing sound from the addressed source: mute, zero output, stop speaking, or stop/pause identified audible playback. Stop alone lacks source evidence. Do not equate all responses/notifications with sound when text/visual modalities are possible.
rules.unmute: An explicit unmute is an audio-control adjustment but not a request for a relative loudness increase or for silence. Actual prior mute state and resulting level are not inferred.
rules.relative_and_target: Decrease to ten percent expresses both relative quieter and adjustment. Set to sixty-five percent expresses adjustment alone. Maximum/high/low are absolute targets unless the utterance also expresses a relative direction.
rules.absence_vs_ambiguity: Unknown physical current state is not unknown semantic evidence. A clearly different act gives false; unresolved domain, act or conflicting direction gives unavailable for the affected predicates only.
rules.information_vs_interface: Ask the current numerical level/mute status for audio_level_information; ask to open/show the settings interface for audio_controls_open. Bare volume settings can mean either; no inference from an opened interface to a current-state question.
rules.no_automatic_closure: Each predicate has its own evidence. Explicit mute may satisfy silence and adjustment; do-not-speak can satisfy silence without adjustment. Broader/narrower vocabulary does not automatically label other predicates.
rules.coexistence: Separate clauses can satisfy different predicates. Contradictory directions in an unresolved fragment do not authorize marking both true; clearly distinct directed operations can coexist.

scope: Task-level audio semantics, no new output coordinates and no environmental state inference. Native labels unchanged.
